dashboard.metaDescription: A free, open source workbench in your browser for learning circuits, boards, robots and drones. Wire parts, run code in a simulator and break things on purpose.
dashboard.title: Learn hardware by *building* it
dashboard.lede: iynk is a browser workbench for learning circuits, boards, robots and drones. You wire the parts, run your own code on a simulated board and see what happens, including when something goes wrong.
dashboard.start: Start with the Arduino Uno R3
dashboard.heroFigure: Arduino Uno R3 running Blink on a breadboard, live: drag to turn it

openSource.title: Open source
openSource.fidelity: iynk runs your code in its own interpreter, not on a real chip. It teaches how parts behave; it does not replace a bench, a compiler or a datasheet.

board.text: From the Arduino Uno R3 to two FPGA boards: lessons, a live code editor, schematic and breadboard views, a serial monitor and failures that really trigger.

robotics.text: Motor drivers, sensors and power stages, built part by part on the bench, with practice tasks, quizzes after each step, live status and current draw.

drones.text: From a Tiny Whoop to an octocopter: a part-by-part build, live weight and thrust maths, safety tests, real Betaflight and ArduPilot settings, and a flying range.

continue.title: Continue where you left off
continue.empty: Nothing finished yet. The Uno R3 is the best place to begin: sixteen short lessons, from the parts of the board to a parking sensor.

see.title: See through it
see.text: Drag to turn any figure all the way round, switch on See-through and watch the parts inside work, with labels that light up.

code.title: Run real code
code.text: Edit Arduino C++, MicroPython or Verilog and press Run: the simulator drives the figure, the pins and the serial monitor.

break.title: Break it on purpose
break.text: Reverse the polarity, brown out the supply, leave out a part or make a cold joint, and see what really goes wrong.

fly.title: Arm and fly
fly.text: Build a drone, check its numbers, run the smoke stopper and motor tests, then fly gates in angle or acro mode.

about.metaDescription: What iynk is, how it works, and the credits and licences behind it.
about.title: About iynk
about.lede: iynk is a hardware lab you open in a browser. Every board, module and drone is a hand-inked 3D figure you can turn, open up and operate, wired to lessons, code that really runs, and failures you can trigger on purpose.

how.figures: Each figure is a self-contained page drawn with the Colorfigures engine: real 3D bodies in flat light, mid and dark bands with ink outlines. The page talks to the figure through a small message bridge, so pressing a button in the lesson moves the part in the figure and the other way round.
how.code: Sketches run in a simulator in your browser on a virtual clock: an Arduino C++ subset with the right integer widths for each chip, a MicroPython subset, and a Verilog subset for the two FPGA boards.
how.privacy: Progress and settings are saved in this browser's local storage. There are no accounts. iynk keeps a local log of what happens in the labs. It stays in this browser, and you can read, copy or clear it under Keys and usage. Nothing is sent to us.

about.originalsLede: iynk was inspired by three teaching sites. It is a separate project with its own code.

arduino.name: Learn Arduino
arduino.text: Sixteen component lessons on the Arduino Uno, with a live code panel, a serial monitor and a schematic view.

robotics.name: Robotics Engineer
robotics.text: Thirteen interactive benches: boards, motor drivers, sensors and power stages, with a build flow, faults and quizzes.

drones.name: Drone Engineer
drones.text: Thirteen drones with part-by-part builds, live calculations, safety tests and a flying range.

about.licenceText: The figures are drawn with Colorfigures by April Zhu, the engine the Robotics Engineer and Drone Engineer sites are drawn with too. Colorfigures builds on ISO-GLOW by April Zhu and iso-figure by Tolga Cohce, and is released under the MIT licence below.
about.licenceNote: The licence is reproduced in its original English.
about.builtWith: Next.js, React and Tailwind CSS (all MIT licensed), plus the Colorfigures engine for every figure.

privacy.metaDescription: What iynk stores in your browser, what it sends and what it never does.
privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.lede: iynk has no accounts, no ads and no analytics. This is a short note on what the app stores and sends. It is not legal advice.

stays.title: What stays in your browser
stays.text: Your progress and settings are saved in this browser's local storage under iynk:v1. The language you pick is remembered in a cookie named iynk-lang. If you add an AI or search key, it is kept under iynk:keys:v1. A local log of what happens in the labs is kept under iynk:log:v1. You can read, copy or clear it under Keys and usage.

leaves.title: What leaves your browser
leaves.text: Nothing, unless you use a room or add a key. A room sends your name, cursor and chat messages, including the text of a voice message, to the room relay. A key you add is sent to your own iynk server with each AI or search call, and a voice recording is sent there to be transcribed. The server does not store the key.

never.title: What we do not do
never.text: There are no accounts, no ads and no analytics. The usage counts are a local log in your browser. You can read it and clear it at any time.
